key_insight: Machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics links aging in amorphous Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ to enhanced axial-bond Peierls distortion, a wider electronic band gap, and reduced atomic mobility.
engineering_relevance: These structural insights help explain resistance drift that degrades the reliability of phase-change memory devices.
method: Simulate amorphous Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ using a machine-learning interatomic potential.
Follow 24 ns of equilibration at 400 K with approximately 100 ns of aging.
Compute electronic band gaps in smaller aged amorphous models using density functional theory.
evidence_signal: The simulations show stronger Peierls distortion and longer bond lifetimes during aging, while DFT calculations associate aging with band-gap widening.
watch_item: Homopolar bonds did not decrease over the simulated interval, leaving longer-timescale structural relaxation unresolved.
paper_title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$
